title: The Morning Road
summary: On the morning after Iron Worm, Gunnar notices that a coffee cart organizes the sidewalk by repetition while Bjorn studies the transaction itself.
settingText: Bushwick sidewalk and street coffee cart, morning
panelPlan: Wide: Morning foot traffic compresses naturally around a small street coffee cart on a familiar Bushwick route. Carrie stops without ceremony; Bjorn and Gunnar stop with her.
Medium: The Coffee Vendor handles three customers in rapid succession, already knowing one person's usual order and waving another forward before the first has fully left.
Close on Gunnar: He watches the flow of people more than the coffee.
Medium on Bjorn: He watches the sequence of order, payment, remembered preference and immediate handoff.
Two-shot: The Coffee Vendor looks directly at Bjorn and waits for his order while the line continues behind him.

dialogueInline.text: The coffee man controls the morning road.
People stop when he tells them to.

source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: The First Cup
summary: Bjorn learns his first coffee preference through an ordinary overly-sweet order, giving the vendor useful information to remember later.
panelPlan: Medium at the cart: Bjorn looks at the cup just handed to the customer ahead of him rather than asking Carrie what to order.
Two-shot: Bjorn indicates the departing customer's cup; the vendor repeats the ordinary order components to confirm.
Insert: The vendor makes Bjorn's coffee and passes it over.
Close: Bjorn tastes it, considers the result seriously, and makes a small dissatisfied face.
Medium: The vendor is already serving the next person but registers Bjorn's verdict.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Again
summary: A later visit takes fewer words because the vendor remembers Bjorn's preference and Bjorn already knows how to move with the line.
panelPlan: Wide: Another morning, different commuters, same cart. Bjorn and Gunnar join the short line without stopping its flow.
Medium: Before Bjorn reaches the window, the Coffee Vendor starts a black coffee.
Close on Gunnar: He notices first.
Medium: Bjorn reaches the window with cash already in hand.
Wide: Bjorn steps away immediately after the handoff, allowing the next customer forward.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Enemy Coffee
summary: The remembered mistake becomes shared neighborhood humor while Gunnar enjoys teasing Bjorn rather than analyzing the city.
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn and Gunnar approach; the Coffee Vendor sees them before they reach the cart.
Two-shot at the service window: The vendor holds up Bjorn's plain black coffee and gestures toward the sweeter order Bjorn rejected on the first visit.
Close on Bjorn: He chooses without hesitation.
Close on Gunnar: He laughs openly at the idea that Bjorn now has an established bad order.
Medium: The vendor passes over the correct cup while the line keeps moving.

dialogueInline.text: Regular, or the one you hated?

source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Bjorn
summary: The vendor uses Bjorn's name for the first time, moving the ritual from remembered preference to remembered person.
panelPlan: Wide: An ordinary morning rush. Carrie is a few steps behind while Bjorn reaches the cart.
Medium: The Coffee Vendor starts the usual cup without asking.
Close: The vendor sets the cup down and addresses Bjorn by name.
Close on Bjorn: He pauses before taking the cup; being named matters more than the coffee.
Medium: The vendor has already turned to the next customer while Bjorn moves aside with the line.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: The Bond
summary: Bjorn interprets repeated accurate recognition as a genuine social bond; Carrie sees only six ordinary coffee orders, and both descriptions are true.
settingText: Bushwick sidewalk beyond the coffee cart, morning
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn, Carrie and Gunnar continue down the sidewalk with Bjorn's coffee; the cart remains busy behind them.
Medium: Bjorn glances back once toward the vendor.
Two-shot: Carrie catches the look and asks what he is doing.
Medium on Bjorn: He states the significance plainly rather than sentimentally.
Wide: They keep walking as the Coffee Vendor serves the next customer in the background.

dialogueInline.text: You ordered the same thing six times.

source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Provisions
summary: After Iron Worm, Gunnar can make a nearby supply run himself; Carrie supplies a short list and cash rather than escorting him through the transaction.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment and neighborhood bodega, daytime
panelPlan: Wide: In 5B, Carrie places a short grocery list and folded cash on the table while the household sorts what remains from breakfast.
Medium: Gunnar reads the list once and pockets the cash.
Two-shot: Bjorn names the practical requirement: enough food that does not depend on a cooking fire.
Exterior wide: Gunnar walks the familiar block alone toward the bodega; no map is open in his hand.
Medium inside bodega: Sal looks up from behind the counter as Gunnar enters, recognizes him from earlier household visits, and returns to what he is doing.

dialogueInline.text: Bread. Meat. Fruit. Something that keeps.

source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: No Questions
summary: Sal translates Gunnar's practical request directly into useful inventory and asks nothing about Gunnar that the transaction does not require.
panelPlan: Medium at the counter: Gunnar gives Sal a concise description of the household need.
Wide aisle view: Sal points out durable ready-to-eat options without leaving the register for long.
Insert: Bread, cheese, dried meat and fruit accumulate in Gunnar's basket; nothing is exotic or ceremonial.
Medium: Gunnar pays with the cash Carrie gave him; Sal counts change normally.
Final medium: Gunnar leaves with the bag. On-page Gunnar observation caption, exactly: "He did not ask questions. I respect this."
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: The Store Has a Shape
summary: Gunnar begins mapping the bodega by usefulness and reliability, including one questionable hot-food tray and the store cat.
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar moves through the bodega with a small folded paper, noting the practical locations of water, bread, dried food, soap, batteries and the counter.
Insert: He marks a small X beside the hot-food case after noticing the same tired tray from an earlier visit.
Medium: Sal catches Gunnar writing while ringing another customer.
Low angle: The bodega cat watches from a shelf near the counter.
Two-shot: Gunnar studies the cat with professional respect while Sal barely looks over.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Sal
summary: The recurring merchant becomes a named person, and Gunnar's map of the neighborhood gains a human relationship rather than just a reliable location.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar waits near the counter while Sal serves another customer.
Insert dialogue moment: The other customer addresses Sal by name while asking for something behind the counter.
Medium: After the customer leaves, Sal turns to Gunnar and reaches for Gunnar's usual durable-food item.
Close on Gunnar: He uses Sal's name for the first time.
Two-shot: Sal answers with Gunnar's name just as casually.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Same
summary: Repeated trade compresses into shorthand as Sal anticipates one of Gunnar's usual purchases before Gunnar asks.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar enters while Sal is restocking near the register.
Insert: Sal places Gunnar's familiar dried-food item on the counter before Gunnar reaches it.
Close on Gunnar: He looks at the item, then at Sal.
Two-shot: Sal keeps working while Gunnar pays.
Wide: Gunnar leaves carrying the same small bag as on prior visits.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Reciprocity
summary: Gunnar decides that repeated useful exchange deserves a small reciprocal gesture beyond payment, without turning the gesture into a speech about friendship.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar sits at the table carving a small simple token from a scrap of clean wood; it is modest, palm-sized and clearly not a major art object.
Close: Bjorn looks over from another household task.
Two-shot: Gunnar keeps carving while answering.
Medium: Astrid passes behind them, sees the token, and understands without joining the discussion.
Insert: Gunnar finishes the small piece and puts it into his coat pocket beside the grocery list.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: The Token
summary: Gunnar leaves the carved token after an ordinary purchase; Sal notices it but refuses to turn the gesture into ceremony.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar arrives and completes the familiar purchase first.
Insert: He places exact payment on the counter.
Close: As Sal bags the item, Gunnar sets the small carved token beside the register.
Close on Sal: He sees it, then looks once at Gunnar.
Wide: Gunnar leaves. Sal turns immediately to the next customer, leaving the token where Gunnar placed it. On-page Gunnar observation caption, exactly: "I have left him a small carved token."
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Respect
summary: On a later visit, Gunnar finds the token still present but still unmentioned; Sal's refusal to perform gratitude makes the relationship feel more trustworthy to him.
panelPlan: Wide: Another normal bodega visit. The carved token now sits unobtrusively near the register, being used to hold down a small stack of receipts.
Medium: Sal puts Gunnar's familiar item on the counter.
Low angle: The bodega cat has moved to a different shelf and watches Gunnar.
Two-shot: Gunnar pays; neither man mentions the token.
Final exterior: Gunnar exits with the bag. On-page Gunnar observation caption, exactly: "He has not acknowledged it. I respect this also."
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Laundry Day
summary: Carrie accompanies Astrid and First Male Kin to the laundromat, where their material-care competence is obvious and the only lesson needed is one piece of local room etiquette.
panelPlan: Wide: Ordinary neighborhood laundromat with plastic folding tables, rolling carts and rows of machines. Carrie enters with Astrid and First Male Kin carrying household laundry.
Medium: Astrid and First Male Kin sort washable cloth from wool, leather and other items that should not enter the machines; they do this without Carrie's help.
Insert: First Male Kin positions the household basket beside a folding table, unintentionally narrowing access to a dryer door.
Medium: The Laundromat Regular with the red rolling cart points to the blocked dryer.
Medium: First Male Kin immediately moves the basket and leaves the access clear.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Four Minutes
summary: The laundromat's unreliable timer becomes a shared modern annoyance rather than a technology lesson.
panelPlan: Insert: A dryer display reads four minutes remaining.
Medium: First Male Kin sits waiting while Astrid folds dry items and Carrie checks her phone.
Insert: Several real minutes later, the same display still reads four.
Close on First Male Kin: He compares the display to the passage of time with calm disbelief.
Medium: The Laundromat Regular answers before Carrie can.

dialogueInline.text: That is not how numbers work.

source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Once Is Enough
summary: On the next laundry visit the household automatically follows the one local correction they received, becoming easier to share the room with.
panelPlan: Wide: Another laundry day. Astrid and First Male Kin enter without Carrie, carrying the same household basket.
Medium: First Male Kin places the basket in the corrected position that leaves the dryer access clear.
Medium: The Laundromat Regular rolls the red cart past them and gives a small greeting, noticing the clear path without commenting on it.
Medium: A different patron briefly blocks the same dryer area with a bag.
Wide: First Male Kin simply works around the obstruction while Astrid folds; nobody turns the moment into a lesson.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Machine Lied Again
summary: Repeated experience turns the bad timer into a shared local joke between First Male Kin and the laundromat regular.
panelPlan: Insert: The familiar dryer display shows four minutes.
Medium: First Male Kin looks at the display, then across the room toward the Laundromat Regular.
Close: The regular sees his expression and already knows the problem.
Two-shot across folding tables: First Male Kin delivers the complaint as established local shorthand.
Wide: Astrid keeps folding while both of them return to their tasks.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: The Spicy Ones
summary: Astrid and the upstairs neighbor develop a tiny reciprocal snack ritual that works through familiarity more than shared language.
panelPlan: Wide: Astrid exits 5B carrying a small packaged snack; the Upstairs Neighbor is locking their own door.
Medium: Without stopping for a formal visit, Astrid offers the package.
Close: The neighbor recognizes the flavor immediately.
Two-shot: The neighbor accepts it while handing Astrid a different packaged snack in return.
Wide: They continue in opposite directions down the hallway.

dialogueInline.text: You always bring the spicy ones.

source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: Known Places
summary: The issue cross-cuts the repeated relationships to show that recognition is now distributed across several ordinary places and requires fewer words each time.
settingText: Bushwick neighborhood cross-cut: coffee cart, bodega, laundromat, apartment hallway
panelPlan: Coffee cart — Medium: The Coffee Vendor begins Bjorn's black coffee before Bjorn reaches the window.
Bodega — Medium: Sal places Gunnar's familiar dried-food item on the counter as Gunnar enters; the carved token remains near the register.
Laundromat — Medium: The Laundromat Regular shifts the red rolling cart to leave the familiar folding space open as First Male Kin arrives.
Hallway — Medium: The Upstairs Neighbor and Astrid pass with a routine greeting, neither slowing down.
Four-way visual rhythm: Each exchange completes with less explanation than it once required.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.

title: The Neighborhood Remembers
summary: Coffee, provisions, folded laundry and exchanged snacks return to one household; Carrie sees a successful ordinary day, while the neighborhood outside has simply begun expecting the Vikings to be there.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment and exterior block at dusk
panelPlan: Wide: Evening in 5B. Bjorn sets down an empty coffee cup; Gunnar unpacks bodega provisions; Astrid places the exchanged snack on a shelf; First Male Kin brings in neatly folded laundry while Second Male Kin helps put it away.
Medium: Carrie arrives or looks up from her folder as the day's ordinary goods settle into the room.
Medium: She asks the simplest possible question and receives a list of equally ordinary answers.
Close: First Male Kin adds the laundromat's one recurring grievance.

Exterior wide: The apartment building and block at dusk. The bodega, coffee cart route, laundromat and neighboring windows continue their own activity. The Vikings are no longer the only story happening here.
source: Issue 5 — The Neighborhood compiled from recovered Coffee Guy / Gunnar-and-Sal / laundry / neighborhood-recognition material and the approved 21-page development outline.
